title: Embedding Multimedia: Audio and Video
ques: Demonstrate the use of HTML5 **`<video>`** and **`<audio>`** elements with fallback `<source>` formats and subtitles/captions via `<track>`.
explanation: The `<video>` and `<audio>` tags natively render media controls without third-party plugins. Multiple `<source>` tags allow browsers to select their best supported codec.

title: Drawing Dynamic Graphics with the Canvas API
ques: Explain the role of the HTML5 **`<canvas>`** element. Write an HTML and JavaScript snippet that gets the 2D rendering context and draws a filled rectangle and circle.

answer.content:
<canvas id="gameCanvas" width="400" height="200" style="border: 1px solid #ccc;">
  Canvas not supported by this browser.
</canvas>

<script>
  const canvas = document.getElementById('gameCanvas');
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');

  // 1. Draw a blue filled rectangle
  ctx.fillStyle = '#2563eb';
  ctx.fillRect(20, 20, 100, 60);

  // 2. Draw a green stroked circle
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.arc(220, 50, 40, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
  ctx.fillStyle = '#10b981';
  ctx.fill();
  ctx.lineWidth = 3;
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#047857';
  ctx.stroke();
</script>

explanation: The `<canvas>` element provides a resolution-dependent bitmap canvas for rendering dynamic 2D shapes, charts, animations, and game graphics via JavaScript.
